patient_info.smoking_history: Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 5 years ago
patient_info.medical_history: COPD, hypertension, no prior cancer history

findings: 4.5 cm spiculated mass in right upper lobe
Mass abuts the pleural surface with possible chest wall invasion
Enlarged right hilar lymph nodes (largest 2.3 cm)
imaging.impression: Suspicious for primary lung malignancy with regional lymph node involvement, clinical Stage IIIA

treatment_plan.approach: Concurrent chemoradiation followed by immunotherapy consolidation
treatment_plan.regimen: Carboplatin/Paclitaxel + radiation 60 Gy, then Durvalumab consolidation

findings: Primary tumor decreased to 2.8 cm (38% reduction)
Post-radiation changes in right upper lobe
Mediastinal lymph nodes significantly decreased (largest now 1.0 cm)
PET: Decreased FDG uptake in primary tumor (SUV 3.2, down from 8.5)
imaging.impression: Partial response to chemoradiation, no evidence of progression

treatment_received.complications: Grade 2 esophagitis, manageable with supportive care

findings: Stable residual mass 2.5 cm in right upper lobe
Mediastinal lymph nodes stable, no pathologic enlargement
No new lesions or distant metastases
imaging.impression: Stable disease, continued response to treatment

clinical_assessment.toxicity: Grade 1 fatigue, no immune-related adverse events

current_treatment.immunotherapy: Durvalumab 10mg/kg IV every 2 weeks (3 months completed)
current_treatment.surveillance_plan: CT chest every 3 months, PET-CT at 12 months

prognosis.progression_risk: Low risk of local recurrence, moderate risk of distant metastasis

treatment_timeline: May 2026: Stable disease, excellent disease control

longitudinal_insights.treatment_effectiveness: Chemoradiation highly effective for local control
